program.name: pong-incoming-twelve-frame-lead-v2
program.guidance:
Which action should align the player paddle with the selected ball target? Read player and ball in observation.objects and motion in observation/history. A bbox is [x, y, width, height]; center height is y + height/2. Larger y means lower. RIGHT moves UP; LEFT moves DOWN. If either object is absent, choose NOOP.
Default to the current ball center. For reliably incoming motion toward the right-side player, predict up to twelve raw frames ahead, covering three decision intervals. Obtain velocity per raw frame from the available history timing; missing velocity is unknown. Estimate time to contact from the horizontal gap between the ball's right edge and the player's left face divided by positive horizontal velocity. Use the smaller of twelve frames and that contact time, with a minimum of zero. The target is current ball center plus vertical velocity times this horizon.
Account for any wall reflection within the prediction only when its boundary and reversal are established by the original observation/history. Never invent wall coordinates. If the longer prediction cannot be resolved because of a possible wall collision, fall back to the previous four-frame prediction, shortened to contact time. If that prediction is also unresolved, use current ball height.
For outgoing motion or uncertain velocity, use current ball height. After a bounce or point reset, discard pre-event velocity until post-event motion is established.
If the target is more than four pixels above player center, choose RIGHT. If more than four pixels below, choose LEFT. Otherwise choose NOOP. Horizontal direction controls prediction, not movement direction. Prefer non-FIRE actions over their movement-equivalent FIRE aliases. Reconsider after each four-raw-frame decision.

action_criteria.NOOP: Choose when player or ball is absent, or the selected target is within four pixels of player center. Use the reliable incoming prediction up to twelve raw frames, capped at contact; fall back to four frames or current height when prediction is unresolved.
action_criteria.FIRE: Stationary alternative when both objects are present and the selected target is within four pixels of player center. It supplies no vertical correction. Prefer NOOP when FIRE has equivalent movement.
action_criteria.RIGHT: Move UP when the selected target is more than four pixels above player center. For reliable incoming motion, use the twelve-frame prediction capped at contact, with the stated uncertainty fallbacks. Otherwise use current ball height. Prefer RIGHT over RIGHTFIRE.
action_criteria.LEFT: Move DOWN when the selected target is more than four pixels below player center. For reliable incoming motion, use the twelve-frame prediction capped at contact, with the stated uncertainty fallbacks. Otherwise use current ball height. Prefer LEFT over LEFTFIRE.
action_criteria.RIGHTFIRE: Upward movement alternative when the selected target is more than four pixels above player center, using the same prediction and fallbacks as RIGHT. Prefer RIGHT when the two actions provide equivalent movement.
action_criteria.LEFTFIRE: Downward movement alternative when the selected target is more than four pixels below player center, using the same prediction and fallbacks as LEFT. Prefer LEFT when the two actions provide equivalent movement.

proposal.hypothesis: Extending reliable incoming-ball anticipation from one decision interval to three may give the paddle more time to reach the arrival region, reducing late interceptions and improving points scored minus conceded.
proposal.operator: Extend the incoming prediction horizon from four to twelve raw frames, still capped at contact time, with the existing short prediction as a fallback when wall behavior makes the longer projection uncertain.
proposal.predicted_changes: During reliable incoming diagonal motion, the paddle should start moving toward future ball heights earlier and may hold or reverse before current-height tracking would. Outgoing and uncertain motion retain current-height tracking. Any improvement in actual point differential remains untested.
proposal.regression_risks: Longer extrapolation amplifies velocity and timing errors. Unrecognized wall reflections can direct the paddle away from contact, while sticky actions can prolong an incorrect correction. Conservative fallback may erase the intended anticipation, and earlier alignment may produce returns that the opponent handles more easily.
